οὐκοῦν τῷ πριαμένῳ δουλεύσωμεν, αὐτῷ παραστήσωμεν ἑαυτοὺς εἰς ὑπακοὴν, "καὶ "τὰ

κατοικεῖ γὰρ ἐν ἁγίοις ἅγιος ὢν κατὰ φύσιν ὡς Θεός. Λέγω δὲ τοῖς ἀγάμοις καὶ ταῖς
χήραις, καλὸν αὐτοῖς ἐστιν ἐὰν μείνωσιν ὡς κἀγώ. Ἐλαφροὶ καὶ εὐπάροιστοι
κατεφωρῶντο λίαν εἰς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν τῶν σφίσι καθ' ἡδονὴν οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραήλ· ταύτῃτοι
δικαίως τὸ χρῆναι γνωμοδοτεῖν παρῄρηντο νόμῳ· ἐπ' αὐτῶν γὰρ, φησὶν, οὐκ ἔστιν

εἰσηγηταὶ βεβηκότα τὸν νοῦν ἔχοντες εἰς τὸ ἀγαθὸν, καὶ αὐτὸν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἐσχηκότες
λαλοῦντα Χριστὸν, ἐθαρσήθησαν εἰκότως 268 ἐπ' ἐξουσίας ποιεῖσθαι πολλῆς τοὺς τῆς
ὑφηγήσεως λόγους, κἂν εἰ μή τι κέοιτο τῶν πρακτέων παρά γε τοῖς ἱεροῖς γράμμασιν·
τοιοῦτός τις ὑπάρχων καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος Λέγω δέ φησι τοῖς ἀγάμοις καὶ ταῖς
χήραις, καλὸν αὐτοῖς ἐὰν μείνωσιν ὡς κἀγὼ, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς· ἔνθα μὲν γὰρ οὐ θεῖος ἡμῖν
νόμος τό Λέγω τέθεικεν ἀναγκαίως· οὗ δὲ Χριστὸς ὁ προστάττων ἦν, τό Παραγγέλλω

νομοθετοῦντι Χριστῷ; ἐπινοοῦσι δὲ τί τὸ ἄμεινον οἱ μυσταγωγοί; καίτοι πῶς οὐκ ἀμαθὲς
καὶ ἀπόπληκτον παντελῶς τὸ μὴ ἀρτίως ἔχειν οἴεσθαι τὰ παρὰ Χριστοῦ; τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν;
οὐκ ἀπέφησεν τὸν γάμον τὸ εὐαγγελικὸν καὶ θεσπέσιον κήρυγμα, ἐπιμετροῦντος οἶμαί

ὁ ἀπολύων "τὴν γυναῖκα "αὐτοῦ παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας, ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι."

pass_a_gloss: [continues from u02-rem-mid: 'the Spirit of adoption has dwelt in us,'] that is, the Holy (Ἅγιον) [Spirit], 'in whom we cry (κράζω) Abba, Father (Πατήρ)'; and we have been bought (ἀγοράζω, pf. pass.) also at a price (τιμή, gen.), Christ the Savior (Σωτήρ) of us all having laid down (τίθημι, pf.) his own soul/life (ψυχή) on behalf of (ὑπέρ) us; we are therefore then temples (ναός) of the living (ζάω) God, for Christ lodges (ἐναυλίζομαι) in us through the Holy Spirit, having in his own nature (φύσις) also the Father and God from whom he has appeared (φαίνω, pf.) essentially (οὐσιωδῶς); for he himself said: 'If anyone loves (ἀγαπάω) me, he will keep (τηρέω) my word (λόγος), and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make (ποιέω) an abode (μονή) with him.' Let then be far (ἄπειμι, impv.) from our thoughts (διάνοια) as from a temple of God the ill-smelling (κάκοσμος) pleasure (ἡδονή), but let rather go up (ἀναφοιτάω, impv.) as in the order (τάξις) of incense offerings (θυμίαμα) the fragrance (εὐοσμία) of self-control (ἐγκράτεια), and let us present (παρίστημι, subj.) 'our bodies a living sacrifice (θυσία), holy, well-pleasing (εὐάρεστος) to God, the rational (λογικός) worship (λατρεία)' of ours; for we were bought 'not with perishable (φθαρτός) silver (ἀργύριον) or gold (χρυσίον) but with precious (τίμιος) blood (αἷμα)', according to what is written (γράφω); so let us serve as slaves (δουλεύω) the one who purchased (πρίαμαι) [us], let us present ourselves to him for obedience (ὑπακοή), 'and our members weapons/instruments (ὅπλον) of righteousness (δικαιοσύνη) to God'; for it is written that 'The body [is] not for fornication (πορνεία) but for the Lord (Κύριος), and the Lord for the body.' When therefore we keep the members of the body not having the defilement (μολυσμός) from love of the flesh (φιλοσαρκία), then also the Lord will be for the body; for he dwells (κατοικέω) among holy ones (ἅγιος), being holy by nature (κατὰ φύσιν) as God. [Lemma:] I say to the unmarried (ἄγαμος) and to the widows (χήρα), it is good for them if they remain (μένω) as I also. Light (ἐλαφρός) and easily goaded (εὐπάροιστος) were they very much detected (καταφωράω, impf. pass.) [to be] toward anything whatever of the things pleasing (καθ' ἡδονήν) to them, those from Israel; for this very reason justly (δικαίως) they had been deprived (παραιρέω, plpf. pass.) by law (νόμος) of the [right] that they should give opinions (γνωμοδοτέω); for upon them, it says, it is not possible to add (προστίθημι), and from them it is not possible to take away (ἀφαιρέω); but the introducers (εἰσηγητής) of the evangelical decrees (θέσπισμα) having the mind (νοῦς) set firm (βαίνω, pf. ptc.) toward the good, and having had in themselves Christ himself speaking (λαλέω), were with reason emboldened (θαρσέω, aor. pass.) to make with much authority (ἐξουσία) the words of guidance (ὑφήγησις), even if something of the things to be done (πρακτέον) should not lie (κεῖμαι) in the sacred writings (ἱερὰ γράμματα); such a one being also the divine (θεσπέσιος) Paul: I say, he says, to the unmarried and the widows, good for them if they remain as I also, and the following; for where a divine law does not [exist] for us, he has necessarily (ἀναγκαίως) set the 'I say'; but where Christ was the one ordering (προστάσσω), he says the 'I command (παραγγέλλω)', adding at once the 'Not I, but the Lord'. But what then of the necessary things has been overlooked (παροράω, pf. pass.) by Christ legislating (νομοθετέω)? And do the mystagogues (μυσταγωγός) devise (ἐπινοέω) something better? And yet how [is it] not ignorant (ἀμαθής) and utterly stupefied (ἀπόπληκτος) to think the things from Christ not to be complete (ἀρτίως ἔχειν)? What then shall we say? The evangelical and divine proclamation (κήρυγμα) did not forbid (ἀπόφημι) marriage (γάμος), God, I think, measuring out (ἐπιμετρέω) the commandment (ἐντολή) to the nature of man; for the Lord said to the Pharisees testing (πειράζω) [him], who asked him 'whether it is lawful (ἔξεστι) to put away (ἀπολύω) his wife' not for fornication, that the one putting away 'his wife apart from (παρεκτός) a matter (λόγος) of fornication makes her commit adultery (μοιχεύω, aor. pass. inf.)'. To these the disciples (μαθητής) say to him: 'If thus is the case (αἰτία) of the man with the wife, it is not expedient (συμφέρει) to marry'; and he said to them: 'There are eunuchs (εὐνοῦχος) who from the mother's womb (κοιλία) were born thus, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs (εὐνουχίζω) by men, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom (βασιλεία) of the heavens; the one able to receive (χωρέω), let him receive.' For he set [it] before (προτίθημι) those willing (ἐθέλω) to achieve (κατορθόω) [it], yet did not bring [it] under (ὑπάγω) law, because he knew that not all are able to prevail over (κατευμεγεθέω) the movements (κίνημα) of the flesh. [Col. 269] And in this altogether (εἰς ἅπαν) the shadow (σκιά) according to the law too has something such; for it ordered the modes (τρόπος) of the sacrifices to be made for the glory of God, this one for sin and ignorances (ἀγνόημα), that one for cleansing (καθαρισμός) and casting away (ἀπόρριψις) of filth (ῥύπος), and moreover those on the Sabbath (σάββατον), those at the new moon (νουμηνία), those at the feasts (ἑορτή); but it permitted (ἀφίημι, impf.) besides these also [continues in u03-open: 'some to make freewill offerings']
pass_b_english: …that is, the Holy Spirit, “by whom we cry, Abba, Father” (Romans 8:15). And we have been bought at a price (1 Corinthians 6:20), since Christ, the Savior of us all, laid down his own life for us (compare 1 John 3:16). We are, then, temples of the living God (2 Corinthians 6:16); for Christ makes his dwelling in us through the Holy Spirit, and in his own nature he has also the Father and God, from whom he came forth in essence. For he himself said, “If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him” (John 14:23).

So let foul-smelling pleasure be far from our minds, as from a temple of God, and let the sweet fragrance of self-control rise up instead, like incense. Let us present “our bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God, our reasonable worship” (Romans 12:1). For we were bought “not with perishable things, with silver or gold, but with precious blood” (1 Peter 1:18–19), as it is written. Let us therefore serve him who bought us; let us present ourselves to him for obedience (Romans 6:16), “and our members as instruments of righteousness to God” (Romans 6:13). For it is written, “The body is not for fornication but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body” (1 Corinthians 6:13). So when we keep the members of the body free of the defilement that comes from love of the flesh, then the Lord too will be for the body; for he dwells among the holy, being holy by nature, as God.
“To the unmarried and the widows I say: it is good for them if they remain as I am” (1 Corinthians 7:8).

The people of Israel were found to be very fickle and easily carried away toward anything at all that pleased them. For this very reason they were rightly barred by the law from giving rulings of their own. For of the commandments it says, “To them nothing may be added, and from them nothing may be taken away” (Ecclesiastes 3:14; compare Deuteronomy 4:2). But those who brought in the decrees of the Gospel had minds set firmly on the good and had Christ himself speaking within them (compare 2 Corinthians 13:3). So they rightly took courage to give their words of guidance with great authority, even where some matter of conduct was not laid down in the sacred writings.

The inspired Paul was such a man. “I say,” he writes, “to the unmarried and the widows, it is good for them if they remain as I am,” and so on (1 Corinthians 7:8). Where we have no divine law, he has of necessity put “I say”; but where Christ was the one giving the command, he says “I command,” adding at once, “not I, but the Lord” (1 Corinthians 7:10). Yet what necessary thing did Christ overlook when he gave the law? Do those who lead us into the mysteries devise something better? And how could it be anything but ignorant and utterly senseless to think that what comes from Christ is not complete? What, then, shall we say?

The divine preaching of the Gospel did not forbid marriage, since God, I think, measures the commandment to human nature. For when the Pharisees, testing him, asked the Lord “whether it is lawful to put away his wife” (Matthew 19:3) for a cause other than fornication, he told them that whoever puts away “his wife, except on the ground of fornication, causes her to commit adultery” (Matthew 5:32; compare Matthew 19:9). At this the disciples said to him, “If this is how the case stands between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry.” And he said to them, “There are eunuchs who were born so from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let the one who is able to accept this accept it” (Matthew 19:10, 12). For he set it before those who wish to achieve it, but he did not bring it under law, since he knew that not all are able to master the impulses of the flesh.

In this the shadow of the law (compare Hebrews 10:1) also has something entirely like it. It commanded that the various kinds of sacrifice be offered to the glory of God: some for sin and for sins of ignorance, others for cleansing and the casting away of filth, and also those on the Sabbath, those at the new moon, and those at the feasts. But besides these it also allowed…

choices.why: Christ has come forth from the Father in essence; the doctrinal point is kept exact.
Worship fitting a rational being, in contrast to animal sacrifice.

bible_refs.note: ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν Ἀββᾶ ὁ πατήρ completes the citation begun at the end of u02-rem-mid (πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν· Αββα ὁ πατήρ).
ἠγοράσμεθα … τιμῆς adapts ἠγοράσθητε γὰρ τιμῆς to the first person.
τεθεικότος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τὴν ἰδίαν ψυχήν echoes ἐκεῖνος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἔθηκεν; compare also John 10:11, 15.
ναοὶ Θεοῦ ζῶντος recalls ἡμεῖς γὰρ ναὸς θεοῦ ἐσμεν ζῶντος; Cyril has the plural.
ἐάν τις ἀγαπᾷ με, τὸν λόγον μου τηρήσει, καὶ ὁ πατήρ μου ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν, καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐλευσόμεθα καὶ μονὴν παρ' αὐτῷ ποιησόμεθα matches John 14:23.
παραστήσωμεν τὰ σώματα ἡμῶν θυσίαν ζῶσαν, ἁγίαν, εὐάρεστον τῷ Θεῷ, τὴν λογικὴν λατρείαν ἡμῶν: Romans 12:1 turned into the first person plural.
οὐ φθαρτοῖς ἀργυρίῳ ἢ χρυσίῳ … ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἵματι from 1 Peter 1:18–19, with ἐλυτρώθητε replaced by Cyril's ἠγοράσθημεν; κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον marks it as a quotation.
παραστήσωμεν ἑαυτοὺς εἰς ὑπακοήν echoes ᾧ παριστάνετε ἑαυτοὺς δούλους εἰς ὑπακοήν; joined to the next clause from 6:13.
τὰ μέλη ἡμῶν ὅπλα δικαιοσύνης τῷ Θεῷ = τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα δικαιοσύνης τῷ θεῷ, first person.
τὸ δὲ σῶμα οὐ τῇ πορνείᾳ ἀλλὰ τῷ κυρίῳ, καὶ ὁ κύριος τῷ σώματι matches 1 Corinthians 6:13b.
Lemma, and repeated by Cyril: λέγω δὲ τοῖς ἀγάμοις καὶ ταῖς χήραις, καλὸν αὐτοῖς ἐὰν μείνωσιν ὡς κἀγώ.

ἐπ' αὐτῶν … οὐκ ἔστιν προσθεῖναι, καὶ ἀπ' αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀφελεῖν matches LXX Ecclesiastes 3:14 (ἐπ' αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν προσθεῖναι, καὶ ἀπ' αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔστιν ἀφελεῖν) except for the plural; the thought of the law forbidding additions is Deuteronomy 4:2 (LXX οὐ προσθήσετε … καὶ οὐκ ἀφελεῖτε), so both are given.
αὐτὸν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἐσχηκότες λαλοῦντα Χριστόν echoes τοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ λαλοῦντος Χριστοῦ.
τὸ Παραγγέλλω … οὐκ ἐγὼ ἀλλ' ὁ Κύριος cites 7:10 (παραγγέλλω, οὐκ ἐγὼ ἀλλ' ὁ κύριος).
τοῖς πειράζουσι φαρισαίοις … Εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀπολῦσαι τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ: Matthew 19:3 (πειράζοντες … εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀνθρώπῳ ἀπολῦσαι τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ), without ἀνθρώπῳ and κατὰ πᾶσαν αἰτίαν.
παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας, ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι is the wording of Matthew 5:32; the setting (answer to the Pharisees) and μὴ ἐπὶ πορνείᾳ belong to Matthew 19:9.
The disciples' reply (19:10) and the eunuch saying (19:12) are quoted; 19:11 is not in Cyril's text.
ἡ κατὰ νόμον σκιά recalls σκιὰν γὰρ ἔχων ὁ νόμος.
